findings.title: D6's unconditional fallback notice asserts false text for derived-verdict-with-findings artifacts
findings.description: D6 fixes a real interaction: with a synthetic finding prepended, `findings` is non-empty, so the current `if result.findings / elif result.fallback_used` chain in `format_review_markdown` (persistence.py) would skip the "Findings Not Parsed" section for a capped degraded PASS. But D6's fix — render the notice "whenever `fallback_used` is set, after any findings" — assumes `fallback_used` has one meaning. The parser sets it in two distinct branches (parsers.py:992 and :1025), and `models.py` explicitly documents that one of them "sets fallback_used=True for a verdict that was genuinely STATED" while the verdict-recovery branch derives a lost verdict *from parsed findings*. For that derived-with-findings shape, D6 would append a section whose fixed reason string says "A verdict of X was parsed, but no findings could be extracted" — both halves false there (the verdict was derived, the findings were extracted), in an artifact where findings render normally above it. This slice exists to make artifacts state truthfully what happened, so a degradation notice that misstates the degradation undercuts it. It also interacts with Part B precisely: a derived PASS (all-PASS findings) over a truncated, tool-less diff gets capped, gains the synthetic finding, and then gains the inaccurate notice. Fix options: key the notice on the specific shape (findings empty vs. present), or parameterize the reason text per shape. SC7 covers only "PASS with fallback_used=True that gets capped" and should add the derived-with-findings case.

findings.title: No new I/O paths; provider silence is handled explicitly rather than defaulted
findings.description: The slice adds no new network or subprocess paths — it reads fields off payloads the existing provider streams already deliver — so the failure-mode bar applies to degradation of existing paths. Those are enumerated with explicit handling: `<synthetic>` placeholders and subagent messages skipped (D8), empty `chunk.model` accumulation degrading to "not reported" with a digest line rather than a fabricated id (D11), Codex's no-report case stated in the artifact without a WARNING, and multi-model runs disclosed in the digest with a WARNING (D12). The hand-built-result convention (`None` vs `[]`, `is None` never `or 0`) matches the existing telemetry precedent in `ReviewResult` and the Run Digest.
